claims.table: S2 Data, age-stratified type 2 diabetes relative risks
claims.population: Austrian inpatients with claims in 2006–2007, grouped by age. The study used ICD-10 E11 to identify type 2 diabetes and excluded patients who died during the period.
claims.limits: These are age-band relative risks from the published co-occurrence analysis. A blank p-value means the supplement did not supply a test result. A row by itself does not establish a supported association. The original ICD-10 category and its same-code U.S. catalog anchor can have different definitions.
claims.coverage: The authors tested 1,051 ICD-10 categories. S2 Data contains rows for a subset of the categories tested. Links use same-code, three-character category anchors.

cohorts.cohortLabel: England CPRD Aurum lung cancer cohort
cohorts.population: 69,674 adults with newly documented lung cancer in England, 2010–2022. Diabetes was defined by a qualifying code recorded before the first lung cancer code.
cohorts.timeWindow: Pre-existing documented T2D at the first recorded lung cancer diagnosis.

groups.present: Eligible adults with newly recorded lung cancer

cohorts.mapping: C34 anchors the paper’s SNOMED CT-defined lung cancer phenotype. The estimate covers the full eligible study cohort.
cohorts.limitations: The denominator comprises lung cancer cases. This study estimate does not supply the diabetes prevalence in people without lung cancer, or a lung-cancer risk ratio.

rows.excerpt: Out of the final study population, 20.9% of people had T2DM.

cohorts.cohortLabel: UK Biobank age- and sex-matched cross-sectional cohort
cohorts.population: 21,935 participants with T2D, matched one-to-one to age- and sex-matched participants without T2D.
cohorts.timeWindow: Recorded diagnoses during the study surveillance period ending in 2019.
cohorts.mapping: The code is a navigation anchor for the study-defined phenotype. Ascertainment used diagnoses and other data sources specific to each condition.
cohorts.limitations: UK Biobank is a volunteer cohort. Matching and comparator selection affect these proportions. The estimates describe documented co-prevalence.

rows.phenotype: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (study definition includes spirometry)

cohorts.population: Adults aged 16 or older with recently diagnosed T2D in English general practices, with up to five diabetes-free comparators matched on age, sex, and practice.
cohorts.timeWindow: Condition recorded in or before 2014 among patients contributing throughout 2014. Study definitions applied additional rules for selected diagnoses.
cohorts.mapping: The ICD-10-CM code is a catalog anchor for the clinical phenotype measured in the study. The source definition governs both conditional rows.
cohorts.limitations: Reported fractions are rounded in the paper. The matched prevalence describes recorded disease history in that year. Use the cited clinical phenotype and cohort for interpretation.

cohorts.population: 169,262 eligible ischemic stroke events in Denmark. The study excluded intracerebral hemorrhage and coexisting type 1 diabetes.
cohorts.timeWindow: Documented type 2 diabetes at an eligible ischemic stroke event.
cohorts.mapping: I63 is the catalog anchor for ischemic stroke in the study. The estimate uses all eligible ischemic events and carries no subtype-specific estimate.
cohorts.limitations: The denominator is events. A patient could contribute more than one event. Case ascertainment used registry diagnoses and glucose-lowering treatment history. The study supplies no stroke-free comparator for this estimate.

rows.excerpt: The study included 169,262 IS events; 24,479 with co-morbid T2D.

cohorts.cohortLabel: Danish early-stage breast cancer and matched comparison cohorts
cohorts.population: Danish women aged 30–99 with incident early-stage breast cancer during 1996–2021, plus matched cancer-free women. The study excluded women with prior diabetes or prior cancer, except nonmelanoma skin cancer.
cohorts.timeWindow: Five years of follow-up starting six months after breast cancer diagnosis or the corresponding matched index date.
cohorts.table: Figure 1 and Results, overall cumulative incidence
cohorts.mapping: C50 anchors early-stage breast cancer survivorship in this cohort. Use the stated landmark, horizon, and eligibility.
cohorts.limitations: These are published cumulative incidences accounting for death as a competing event. This estimate describes newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes during follow-up. It does not provide diabetes prevalence at diagnosis.

cohorts.cohortLabel: Kangbuk Samsung Health Study · 2-year cumulative incidence
cohorts.population: 97,347 Korean women with at least one previous birth and no diabetes at entry. The study measured NAFLD by ultrasound and ascertained prior gestational diabetes by self-report.
cohorts.timeWindow: 2 years after the baseline health screening. Enrollment was 2015–2019 and follow-up ran through December 2020.

groups.neither: Women with neither prior gestational diabetes nor NAFLD
groups.gdm_only: Women with prior gestational diabetes and no NAFLD
groups.nafld_only: Women with NAFLD and no prior gestational diabetes
groups.both: Women with both prior gestational diabetes and NAFLD

cohorts.mapping: The same joint estimate is linked to Z86.32 (history of gestational diabetes) and K76.0 (fatty liver anchor). The source used ultrasound-defined NAFLD after excluding secondary causes. O24.4 is the pregnancy diagnosis category.
cohorts.limitations: The publication reports cumulative incidence per 1,000 people. These values are converted to probabilities by dividing by 1,000. Each estimate requires both baseline exposure states.

rows.phenotype: Prior gestational diabetes and ultrasound-defined NAFLD
rows.tableRow: 2-year cumulative incidence per 1,000, four exposure groups

rows.phenotype: Prior gestational diabetes and ultrasound-defined NAFLD
rows.tableRow: 2-year cumulative incidence per 1,000, four exposure groups

cohorts.cohortLabel: Kangbuk Samsung Health Study · 5-year cumulative incidence
cohorts.population: 97,347 Korean women with at least one previous birth and no diabetes at entry. The study measured NAFLD by ultrasound and ascertained prior gestational diabetes by self-report.
cohorts.timeWindow: 5 years after the baseline health screening. Enrollment was 2015–2019 and follow-up ran through December 2020.

groups.neither: Women with neither prior gestational diabetes nor NAFLD
groups.gdm_only: Women with prior gestational diabetes and no NAFLD
groups.nafld_only: Women with NAFLD and no prior gestational diabetes
groups.both: Women with both prior gestational diabetes and NAFLD

cohorts.mapping: The same joint estimate is linked to Z86.32 (history of gestational diabetes) and K76.0 (fatty liver anchor). The source used ultrasound-defined NAFLD after excluding secondary causes. O24.4 is the pregnancy diagnosis category.
cohorts.limitations: The publication reports cumulative incidence per 1,000 people. These values are converted to probabilities by dividing by 1,000. Each estimate requires both baseline exposure states.

rows.phenotype: Prior gestational diabetes and ultrasound-defined NAFLD
rows.tableRow: 5-year cumulative incidence per 1,000, four exposure groups

cohorts.cohortLabel: Finnish national birth and health registers
cohorts.population: 462,401 women with deliveries in Finland, including 96,353 with gestational diabetes and 366,048 without. Subsequent type 2 diabetes was identified using E11 or T90.
cohorts.timeWindow: Follow-up began at first recorded delivery during 2006–2020. Mean follow-up was 6.86 years with gestational diabetes and 9.07 years without it.
cohorts.mapping: Z86.32 is the history anchor. O24.4 marks the pregnancy diagnosis category.
cohorts.limitations: These are observed fractions across unequal follow-up periods. They cannot supply a fixed-horizon conditional distribution.

cohorts.cohortLabel: UK Biobank age- and BMI-matched comparisons
cohorts.population: 1,008 women with previous PCOS and 5,017 matched controls. Median age was 61 years. The PCOS definition used diagnostic coding, self-report, or combined clinical or biochemical findings.
cohorts.timeWindow: Type 2 diabetes recorded at UK Biobank baseline assessment.
cohorts.design: Baseline analysis in a matched cohort
cohorts.mapping: E28.2 anchors study-defined PCOS. The paper's phenotype included qualifying participants without a PCOS code.
cohorts.limitations: The baseline comparison describes a selected, older cohort matched on age and BMI.

cohorts.population: 9,181 patients with STEMI or non-STEMI who survived the index hospitalization and had a known diabetes status, excluding patients with type 1 diabetes and the 2005 extension sample.
cohorts.timeWindow: Type 2 diabetes status at admission for an eligible acute MI.

groups.present: Eligible acute MI patients who survived hospitalization

cohorts.mapping: I21 anchors the pooled STEMI and non-STEMI population. The estimate has no subtype-specific result.
cohorts.limitations: Selection required survival to discharge. The study has no MI-free group for this estimate.

rows.phenotype: Acute MI with survival to discharge
rows.tableRow: Total analyzed and groups by diabetes status

cohorts.cohortLabel: US Clarivate linked claims and medical records, 2017–2022
cohorts.population: 4,657,412 adults with a first recorded MI in the dataset after exclusion of known prior MI. Median age was 70.
cohorts.timeWindow: Type 2 diabetes documented before the first recorded myocardial infarction.

groups.present: Adults with a first recorded MI in the linked dataset

cohorts.mapping: I21 anchors the study's first recorded MI phenotype.
cohorts.limitations: The fraction is based on existing documentation within the linked database. Out-of-hospital fatal first events and patients without care in the dataset may be missed. The paper provides no MI-free denominator.

rows.tableRow: Documented standard modifiable risk factors, type 2 diabetes

cohorts.cohortLabel: Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities and Sleep Heart Health Study
cohorts.population: 1,453 US adults without baseline diabetes, mean age 63 years, with in-home polysomnography and annual follow-up interviews.
cohorts.timeWindow: Sleep testing in 1996–1998 followed by diabetes ascertainment by telephone through 2013. Median follow-up was 13 years.

groups.present: Participants with AHI of at least 5 events per hour
groups.absent: Participants with AHI below 5 events per hour

cohorts.mapping: G47.33 is the obstructive sleep apnea anchor. The present group pools mild (78/418), moderate (48/187) and severe (29/83) apnea strata.
cohorts.limitations: These fractions summarize recorded events during observed follow-up. Severe apnea versus normal had an adjusted hazard ratio of 1.71 (95% CI 1.08–2.71), a separate measure from these fractions.

rows.tableRow: Participant and incident diabetes counts by AHI

cohorts.cohortLabel: Danish Centre for Strategic Research in Type 2 Diabetes
cohorts.population: 11,369 people with recently diagnosed type 2 diabetes enrolled from Danish primary care and hospitals. The kidney estimate uses the subset with qualifying laboratory data.
cohorts.timeWindow: Comorbidity history and measurements at cohort enrollment, 2010–2023.

groups.present: DD2 participants with recently diagnosed type 2 diabetes

cohorts.limitations: The study has no comparison group without diabetes at enrollment. The estimates use recorded comorbidities or available tests.

rows.mapping: I50 is the broad heart-failure anchor. The estimate uses hospital diagnoses and does not resolve subtype.
I25 is a navigation anchor for a broader hospital-recorded ischemic heart disease phenotype. The paper's row is not a prevalence estimate for the ICD-10-CM I25 code itself.

rows.phenotype: Kidney disease by eGFR or albuminuria
rows.mapping: N18 is a clinical anchor. The paper uses eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² or urine albumin-creatinine ratio above 30 mg/g. The denominator is 10,417 with data.
